plain: A natural tendency to act a certain way

webster.text: Bent of mind, natural or acquired; inclination; in a moral sense: disposition to any thing good or evil, particularly to evil; as a propensity to sin; the corrupt propensity of the will.

example.quote: The necessity of a general Govt. proceeds from the propensity of the States to pursue their particular interests in opposition to the general interest.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, July 17, 1787
